1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C ) has been filed by petitioners seeking quashing of the FIR bearing No. 21/2003, registered at Police Station Kanhawala, Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC ) and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Satish Kumar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
5. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Rahul Sharma and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Sandeep from Police Station Kanhawala, Delhi.
6. Brief facts of the present case are that on 10.02.2000, the marriage was solemnized between petitioner and respondent no. 2, according to Hindu Rites and Ceremony.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.
Due to matrimonial disputes, the parties could not stay together and started living separately since 2003.

On the complaint of respondent no. 2, the present FIR bearing No. 21/2003 was registered at Police Station Kanhawala, Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC against the petitioners.

On 09.09.2017, the petitioner no 1 and the respondent Deshraj Chauhan & Anr vs State & Anr on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161367965/
1 no.2 arrived to a compromise and the matter have been settled amicably and the respondent no.2 have settled all her grievances against the petitioners and decided to dissolve the marriage with mutual consent and joint statement was recorded.

entities.text: Deshraj Chauhan & Anr vs State & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 22.12.2017, mediation was held between the respondent no. 2 and the petitioners, whereby the respondent no. 2. has agreed to co- operate him getting the FIR quashed by the Hon ble High Court, Delhi.

7. On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2, who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into a compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties.

8. It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner.
9. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received all the amounts as per settlement and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

10. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion and also the fact that the present matter is a family matter,
this Court is of the opinion that no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
Moreover, there is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

11. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 21/2003, registered at Police Station Kanhawala, Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
12. The present petition stands disposed of.
13. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J APRIL 20, 2023/zp
